title: Tenali Raman and the Master of Disguise
summary: A brilliant actor and linguist named Bahurupi Govinda arrived at the court of Vijayanagara, boasting that he was an absolute master of disguise. He challenged King Krishnadevara...
full_text:
A brilliant actor and linguist named Bahurupi Govinda arrived at the court of Vijayanagara, boasting that he was an absolute master of disguise.
He challenged King Krishnadevaraya:
'Your Majesty! For seven days, I will walk through your court and city in seven different disguises—as a beggar, a merchant, an astrologer, a soldier, a monk, a physician, and a woman.
If your famous wit Tenali Raman cannot unmask me on any day, you must award me five hundred gold coins!'

Tenali accepted the wager.
On the first day, a beggar asked for alms; Tenali looked into his eyes and said: 'Greetings, Govinda!'
On the second day, a physician offered herbs; Tenali unmasked him immediately by his gait.
On the third, fourth, fifth, and sixth days, Tenali penetrated every disguise through careful observation.

On the seventh day, a dignified scholar from Kashmir arrived, speaking impeccable classical Kashmiri, wearing authentic northern furs, debating Sanskrit with profound erudition.
The King was convinced this was a real northern scholar, and even Tenali could find no flaw in his accent, clothing, or behavior!
The sun was setting, and the court prepared to declare Govinda victorious.

As the Kashmiri scholar bowed low to the King to conclude the audience, Tenali Raman quietly slipped behind him, holding a small brass vessel of ice-cold mountain spring water.
Without warning, Tenali dumped the freezing water down the back of the scholar’s neck!

The scholar leaped into the air like a scalded cat, clutching his wet neck, and shouted in fluent, unvarnished, colloquial local **Telugu**:
*‘AYYO! AMMA! WHO POURED COLD WATER DOWN MY SHIRT?’*

The entire court erupted in roaring laughter!
Govinda stood soaked and sheepish, realizing that his native tongue had betrayed him!

Tenali smiled with dazzling triumph:
'Maharaj, a man may master ten foreign languages and practice seventy disguises, but when struck by sudden pain or cold water, he always cries out in his mother tongue!'

The actor bowed low, laughing in admiration:
'Tenali Raman, thou art truly invincible! No disguise can deceive thy understanding of human nature!'
The King rewarded both Tenali and the actor for an unforgettable demonstration of psychology and wit.
moral: An actor may change his costume and accent, but his native tongue betrays him in moments of sudden surprise.
